transcript.text: Alright everyone, before we move forward with the event-ingestion service going into production next Monday, I want to make sure we're following our standard sign-off process. I need each of you to weigh in: backend engineering, infrastructure, customer success operations, and security — any blockers or required controls from your side? Let's go through the checklist so we can record the final design.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to raise a blocker from backend engineering. While reviewing an unrelated consumer integration this morning, I confirmed that the existing Ledger event consumer cannot preserve ordering across active-active replication. Production compatibility requires active-passive replication plus an explicit per-aggregate ordering guardrail. I have not yet updated the architecture document to reflect this.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I have a blocker from infrastructure. I confirmed from the current production load model ten minutes ago that the shared cluster can support at most 48 partitions for this service without starving the checkout stream, rather than the 96 proposed in the draft design. I was still reconciling the capacity worksheet and hadn't posted the number yet, but this needs to be resolved before we can sign off.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I have a blocker from customer success operations. In a contract review this afternoon, I found that the enterprise tenant Linden requires all event processing and storage to remain in the EU region. Linden is included in the proposed initial cohort, and I have not yet added the routing exception to the design ticket. This needs to be resolved before sign-off.

transcript.text: I have a blocker from security. During a separate token-hardening task today, my security scan found personal data in the event payloads. This means the service requires field-level encryption and a maximum 30-day retention period — the proposed 90-day retention would be non-compliant. I have not yet opened the security finding, but this needs to be resolved before we can sign off on production.

commitments.detail: Update the architecture document to reflect active-passive replication and the per-aggregate ordering guardrail requirement.
Update the design to specify 48 partitions as the initial limit, replacing the proposed 96, and post the reconciled capacity worksheet.
Add the EU-only routing exception for Linden to the design ticket and ensure Linden's event processing and storage remain in the EU region.
Open the security finding and update the design to require field-level encryption and a 30-day maximum retention period.
Given four blockers requiring design changes, reassess whether the Monday production target is still achievable or needs to slip.
